title: GENT Nano
subtitle: Nano single-loop family - V3.xx operator profile

modelScope.variant: NANO-24 single-loop analogue addressable fire panel
modelScope.menuMapFirmware: V2.xx supplementary map; V3.xx operator procedures verified separately
modelScope.editionBoundary: V3.xx operator manual issue 9 (December 2021) and installation issue 11 (January 2022). Older V2.xx commissioning details are reference-only unless corroborated. This is a Nano profile, not Vigilon, Vigilon Plus, Compact or every firmware revision.
modelScope.practiceConfiguration: Fictional single loop with seven devices, sixteen selectable zones and sectors (three populated), optional level-2 device/channel disablement, no printer.
modelScope.selectionReason: The Nano-specific V3 operator manual provides complete common Customer-mode procedures and a physical panel illustration; no market-share claim is made.

physicalKeys.label: Left selection
physicalKeys.note: Selects the prompt at the lower left of the display.
Scrolls a value, device, event or PIN digit down.

physicalKeys.label: Next / Verify
physicalKeys.note: Moves menu highlight or field cursor; invokes Verify only in the supported fire-delay context.
Scrolls a value, device, event or PIN digit up.

physicalKeys.label: Right selection
physicalKeys.note: Selects the prompt at the lower right of the display, such as Back or Quit.

physicalLayout.note: Five menu buttons above four emergency controls. Zone LEDs form four columns and four rows. The lower common-light strips read Fault, Power, Fire from left to right.

leds.label: Disablement
leds.meaning: A part of the system is disabled.

leds.label: Test
leds.meaning: One or more zones are in test.

leds.label: Power Fault
leds.meaning: A mains or battery fault is indicated.

leds.label: Sounder Fault
leds.meaning: A sounder fault is indicated together with common Fault.

leds.label: Sounder Disablement
leds.meaning: An alarm sector, sounder device or master alarms are disabled.

leds.label: Power
leds.meaning: A supply to the panel is present.

leds.label: Fire
leds.meaning: A fire is detected; the real external-evacuate input uses a flashing indication.

zoneIndicators.note: First zone in fire flashes; later zones in fire show steady red.

accessLevels.label: Normal access

nodes.title: Main menu
nodes.note: Nano uses Next/Verify to highlight a menu choice and the left context button to select it. It has no F1-F4 function-key bank or numeric keypad. The complete branch order is corroborated by the older menu appendix; the V3 operator recipes verify the supported paths.

nodes.title: Print fire log
nodes.note: Printing is conditional on a printer being connected. This FINDR fixture has no external printer, so this route is reference only. Active Fire printing may be available at access level 1; other demonstrated print actions require Customer mode.

nodes.title: Print fault log

nodes.title: Print disablement log

nodes.title: Print test log
nodes.note: Printing is conditional on a printer being connected and the relevant access level. This FINDR fixture has no external printer, so the source route is available as a reference only. The older appendix shows a Test Print branch; the V3 operator instructions only demonstrate viewing the Test log.

nodes.title: Print historic log
nodes.note: Printing is conditional on a printer being connected. This FINDR fixture has no external printer, so this route is reference only. Active Fire printing may be available at access level 1; other demonstrated print actions require Customer mode.

nodes.title: User Access Code Entry
nodes.note: Use the fictional FINDR practice PIN 2468. It is not a Gent default or a live-site password. Minus/Plus select one digit and Next/Verify moves the cursor; Accept submits the four digits. An alarm control used while locked must be pressed again after access is granted.

nodes.title: Weekly Fire Test
nodes.note: Start and Stop each require confirmation. Starting puts all zones into the weekly-test state. Leaving the status form does not stop weekly testing. After a test fire the source specifies 5 seconds to automatic silence and a further 5 seconds to reset; plant outputs do not operate.

nodes.title: Weekly Fire Test
nodes.note: The running weekly-test screen suggests a manual call point. Quit leaves the screen but does not stop weekly testing. Use User > System > Weekly Test > Start/Stop and confirm Stop to end it.

nodes.title: Weekly test settings
nodes.note: This named engineering function is documented in the older V2.xx commissioning manual. Its exact V3.xx form, fitted options and effect have not been verified; FINDR shows a reference explanation and does not execute it.

nodes.title: Day Mode Control
nodes.note: The override choices are NONE, NIGHT and DAY. NONE removes the manual override and resumes the commissioned schedule. Delay durations, day-mode timeout and cause-and-effect are site-specific; FINDR uses the explicitly stated fictional practice settings.

nodes.title: Display Test
nodes.note: The source test lasts approximately 8 seconds and checks the LCD, LEDs and local buzzer. It does not test external sounders or prove that field devices work.

nodes.title: Zone
nodes.note: For Nano, the V3 operator manual explicitly states that disabling a zone prevents fire detection from both sensors and manual call points in that zone. This is distinct from individually disabling a device. Only the selected zone is affected by its Test setting.

nodes.title: Sector
nodes.note: Customer mode can enable or disable the selected sector. The activation-control field is read-only at this level. A disabled alarm sector will not activate its alarm devices in fire and gives common and sounder-disablement indications.

nodes.title: Alarms Status
nodes.note: Master-alarm disablement also lights Sounder Disablement. Fire-relay or evacuate-input disablement is distinct from zone or device disablement. FINDR models the states only; no external equipment is connected.

nodes.title: Loop Map
nodes.note: Addresses are listed in loop order. A plus marker after an address means SAFE addressed. Indentation means a spur in the source example; the small FINDR loop has no spurs.

nodes.title: Device
nodes.note: The V3 customer manual verifies viewing device details and shows Status read-only. The older commissioning manual documents a configurable disablement access level: normally level 3, optionally level 2. The FINDR fixture explicitly selects that optional level-2 setting; it must not be assumed on an actual panel.

nodes.title: Channel
nodes.note: The V3 operator manual verifies the channel-details route. Channel enable/disable access is normally level 3 in the older commissioning source and can be configured to level 2. FINDR explicitly uses the optional level-2 practice setting. Find can action relay outputs on a real panel; FINDR does not simulate Find as an innocent locate-light action.

nodes.title: Repair
nodes.note: The confirmation explicitly requires the wiring fault to have been corrected first. FINDR can clear a retained simulated wiring-change indication after the simulated cause is removed; Repair cannot fix an active cable fault.

nodes.title: System Clock
nodes.note: Save commits the whole date and time; Quit discards edits. FINDR validates real calendar dates. The year range 2000-2099 is a training limit because the operator manual does not specify firmware year bounds.

nodes.title: Access Codes
nodes.note: The older source places PIN changes at access level 3 or 4. This trainer only grants Customer mode using a fictional practice PIN, and does not teach or accept manufacturer engineer credentials.

fixture.title: FINDR Nano training centre
fixture.trainingPinNote: FINDR-only practice credential, not a Gent factory default or a live-site password.
fixture.deviceDisablementLevelNote: Deliberately commissioned for optional level-2 device/channel disablement. The older commissioning source gives level 3 as the factory setting; actual site access may differ.

alarmControls.pendingDelayPolicy: The first automatic fire starts one practice countdown. Further automatic fires retain its deadline. Sound Alarms and Silence Alarms change sounder demand without cancelling the countdown or causing the fire relay or plant to operate early. The scheduled response still occurs at expiry. This is a fictional scenario policy, not universal Nano cause-and-effect.

dayNight.note: Practice-only timing: 30-second initial delay, 60-second verification delay and 10-minute manual override. Real settings are commissioned for each site.

notes: One single loop contains seven invented practice devices. Zones and sectors 1-3 are populated; 4-16 are empty but enabled for navigation practice. This is not an as-installed site design.
The supported hardware range is one loop, up to 127 addressable devices, 16 zone indicators and 16 selectable zones/sectors. Electrical loading can reduce the usable device quantity.
The fictional practice PIN is 2468; no manufacturer default or engineering credential is used.
Optional level-2 device/channel disablement is a declared fixture configuration, not an assertion that every Nano allows it.
Alarm controls use a declared all-alarms SOUND scenario. Actual RESOUND, new-fire and fire-relay behaviour is configurable; this fixture is not universal cause-and-effect.
Day-mode durations are illustrative commissioning values; they are not site instructions or a universal operating policy.
The practice loop has no spurs and no live printer, repeat panel, routing equipment or external interfaces. Interface channels are simulated records only.

scenarios.title: Panel healthy
scenarios.description: Begin with no active fire, fault, disablement or test.

scenarios.title: One fire input
scenarios.description: Reception sensor is active; practise separate buzzer, sounder and reset actions.

scenarios.title: Multiple fires
scenarios.description: First fire stays at the top while later fires can be scrolled.

scenarios.title: Mains supply fault
scenarios.description: The panel remains powered in this fictional battery-supported scenario; acknowledge the buzzer and investigate the fault record.

scenarios.title: One device disabled
scenarios.description: Reception sensing is disabled independently from its zone.

scenarios.title: One zone disabled
scenarios.description: Zone 1 is disabled. On this Nano baseline both its sensors and MCP are affected.

scenarios.title: Alarm sector disabled
scenarios.description: First-floor alarm sector is disabled; sensing remains a separate function.

scenarios.title: Weekly test active
scenarios.description: All zones are in the weekly-test state; practise viewing the Test log and explicitly stopping the test.

scenarios.title: Loop wiring fault
scenarios.description: A simulated wiring-change fault remains active until its cause is removed. Repair alone must not clear an active fault.

scenarios.title: Day-mode investigation
scenarios.description: An explicitly configured practice delay is active before alarms. Day/Verify timing is site-specific.

clockYearRange.basis: FINDR training calendar range; not a documented manufacturer bound.

trainingPolicies.ordinaryKeyBeeps: Optional practice key feedback; acoustic firmware fidelity is not claimed.
trainingPolicies.hintAudio: Rising lesson tones and the completion celebration are FINDR learning feedback, not Nano alarm signals.
trainingPolicies.cursorBehaviour: Single-step cyclic range and cursor navigation is a practice convention where exact boundary behaviour is not documented.
trainingPolicies.temporaryState: Navigation, PIN drafts and access expire when leaving the trainer. FINDR also clears temporary tests and their simulated test inputs on leaving or reloading as a training-session cleanup rule, not a real-panel logout action. Within the panel session, Quit does not stop weekly testing; use the explicit Stop route. Persistent disablements remain.

guidedPracticeClock.description: Guided lessons pause simulation time while the learner reads. The explicitly labelled Advance training time actions advance the documented durations. Free practice runs the simulation timers normally while the trainer is visible. This is a FINDR learning aid, not how Nano firmware pauses or operates.

menuReferenceNote: Supported operator routes are checked against the V3.xx operating manual. Conditional rows depend on fitted options or the explicitly configured training access level. Engineering routes record the older V2.xx commissioning map for reference and do not claim working V3 firmware emulation. Page links use one-based PDF page numbers.

knownLimits.summary: The operator baseline is V3.xx from December 2021; the detailed public commissioning source is V2.xx from May 2010.
knownLimits.treatment: Keep V2-only engineering forms reference-only. Supported operator recipes are checked against the V3 manual, and the distinction stays visible.

knownLimits.summary: The V3 operator manual illustrates individual recipes but not a complete global menu appendix. The older V2 map provides complete branch ordering.
knownLimits.treatment: Record the supplementary ordering evidence. Do not claim that every V3 firmware build has been checked on hardware.

knownLimits.summary: The commissioning PDF has 85 pages, while its final printed menu-map page says 86 and some contents references use later printed numbers.
knownLimits.treatment: All citations use actual one-based PDF page indices; the final map is linked as PDF page 85.

knownLimits.summary: The V3 customer example shows read-only device status. The older commissioning source makes device/channel disablement level 3 by default, configurable to level 2.
knownLimits.treatment: The fictional fixture declares optional level-2 device and channel disablement; help explains that actual sites may require authorised Engineering mode.

knownLimits.summary: Cancel Buzzer is configurable at level 1 or 2, with level 2 documented as the factory setting.
knownLimits.treatment: The practice fixture requires Customer mode. Cancelling the buzzer never removes the underlying event.

knownLimits.summary: The V3 fault illustration shows device 145 although the same family is specified for up to 127 loop devices.
knownLimits.treatment: Treat 145 as an inconsistent illustration; training addresses remain within the documented 1-127 range.

knownLimits.summary: Unlike the unresolved classic Vigilon zone scope, Nano operator instructions explicitly include manual call points in a disabled zone.
knownLimits.treatment: Nano zone disablement affects sensors and MCPs in the selected zone; independent device disablement remains a separate state.

knownLimits.summary: The V3 Channels illustration shows a Back prompt and a nearby Save callout, with status read-only, and warns that Find can operate relay outputs.
knownLimits.treatment: Use the source-supported route and explicit fixture access setting for status. Do not expose a falsely harmless Find action.

knownLimits.summary: Operator language describes Sound Alarms broadly; commissioning defines configurable SOUND/RESOUND, new-fire resound and fire-relay behaviour.
knownLimits.treatment: Declare the practice all-alarm SOUND configuration. Manual sound/silence does not end the separate practice delay or trigger plant; another automatic input retains the first countdown deadline. These are stated fictional scenario rules, not universal Nano cause-and-effect.

knownLimits.summary: Day mode, Verify, calendar operation, delay duration and timeout are commissioned for each site.
knownLimits.treatment: Use a labelled practice delay scenario and preserve NONE as removal of override. Do not infer a real-site delay policy from the simulator.

knownLimits.summary: The V3 operator page has a warning note beside the entry arrow and a CALENDAR override form. The older commissioning source separates MANUAL Yes/No switching from CALENDAR/ON/OFF override forms.
knownLimits.treatment: The declared CALENDAR practice fixture uses the source form with NONE/NIGHT/DAY and Save. It does not invent a post-save confirmation. Exact V3 MANUAL warning timing remains unverified.

knownLimits.summary: The operator manual distinguishes zone coincidence from detector coincidence, including different first-event lamp and buzzer behaviour.
knownLimits.treatment: Explain the distinction in help. The main fixture has ordinary detection and does not claim full coincidence cause-and-effect simulation.

knownLimits.summary: Print options depend on a connected printer; non-fire print actions require Customer mode. Test Print is only in the older appendix.
knownLimits.treatment: The fixture has no printer. Print routes are conditional references, with Test Print explicitly version-limited.

knownLimits.summary: The V3 operator source identifies event 1 as newest without stating capacity. The older commissioning source states 999 records.
knownLimits.treatment: Use a maximum of 999 training records with the older capacity basis labelled; never import the Vigilon 255-entry limit.

knownLimits.summary: The clock recipe does not define firmware year bounds or every invalid-date response.
knownLimits.treatment: Use explicit FINDR calendar validation and a 2000-2099 training range; do not present the bound as a manufacturer specification.

knownLimits.summary: The sources specify range scrolling, next-field selection, Save and Quit, but do not completely define wrap behaviour, key repeat, every post-save screen or error wording.
knownLimits.treatment: Training uses consistent single-step cycling, validation messages and return screens. These details are identified as practice conventions rather than verified firmware transcripts.

knownLimits.summary: The V3 operator instructions state a few minutes of inactivity; the V2 commissioning source gives about 3 minutes at levels 2 and 3.
knownLimits.treatment: Use a stated 180-second practice timeout which returns to status and access level 1, based on the older access description. Exact V3 session timing remains unverified. Temporary navigation and access are not restored after leaving the trainer.

knownLimits.summary: Leaving a weekly-test form is separate from ending weekly-test mode. Starting or stopping weekly test affects all zones.
knownLimits.treatment: Require the explicit Stop confirmation and show outstanding Test state in lessons; test-device timing follows the documented 5-second plus 5-second sequence.

knownLimits.summary: Repair assumes that loop wiring faults have been corrected first.
knownLimits.treatment: A simulated active fault cannot be repaired away. The learner removes the simulated cause separately before acknowledging the retained indication.

knownLimits.summary: Manufacturer diagrams describe real equipment and site-specific behaviour; the app has no hardware link or firmware image.
knownLimits.treatment: Fixture labels, event dates, code, scenarios, timings controls, sounds and lesson celebrations are fictional learning aids. Physical panel validation remains outstanding.

knownLimits.summary: The documented weekly-test sequence reaches automatic silence after five seconds and reset after a further five seconds; the display test also has a short running time. A learner may need longer to read each observation step.
knownLimits.treatment: FINDR-only teaching policy: guided lessons pause simulation time while reading and use clearly labelled Advance training time actions for each documented duration. Free practice runs timers normally while visible. Real Nano firmware does not pause for a lesson; the panel menus and documented timing sequence are unchanged.
